## Design

### 2026-11-05: At the start of this session, I did a lot of research on what components I should use. This isn't something I've done much of because I've been following a lot of starter projects, so it took me a whi

**7h**

At the start of this session, I did a lot of research on what components I should use. This isn't something I've done much of because I've been following a lot of starter projects, so it took me a while. I was originally planning on using a seperate charging circuit and voltage converter, but I ended up finding an ESP32 devboard that has both of these integrated, so all I have to do is connect the battery to it and it should all work. I chose to go with an 18650 battery for this project because I already have some and they have good capacity. I also chose a 2.4 in tft screen for the display.

Most components I'm using don't have Kicad files, so I had to make my own. I had to do this for the esp32 devboard, the screen, and the toggle switch that I'm using for power. Figuring out the spacings for all the pins was pretty hard because I had to look up the documents with the components dimensions to properly model them. The devboard I'm using doesn't give exact dimensions or pin spacings, so I assumend it uses standard arduino dupont spacing. This took me a while because I don't have much experience doing this, but I think they ended up pretty good.

After this, i started wiring up the schematic. I had to do a good bit of research about which pins of the esp32 I could connect to because the listing for the devboard I'm using wasn't very descriptive. I ended up needing pullup resistors for 4/7 of the buttons because they are connected to pins that don't have internal pullups. I also went ahead and wired up the sd card portion of the screen even though I don't plan on using it, Just in case.

Overall, I'm really enjoying making a project without a beginner's guide. I think its really cool to see everything I've learned over the past 4 weeks come to help me design my very own project from scratch! Although it's taking a lot longer than it did with the guides, I am very happy with the progress I've made so far and can't wait to continue this project!
